slides.title: Scan to open the teacher app

steps.h: Point your camera at the code
steps.b: Or type athleticsos.io/teacher.
School email, then your grade PIN.
Same Teacher Check-In app this walkthrough covers.

slides.note: Hold here until every phone shows the teacher app.

cards.b: HR for academics and BC for behavior. Everyone starts green; mark exceptions.
Submitted marks determine the next status and the family email.

steps.b: The one the school has on file. If you co-teach, either teacher’s email works — you both see the same students.
Shared by grade level, not per person. Ask the office if you do not have it.
On your own laptop or phone you will usually stay signed in week to week.

slides.title: Choose the week and mark exceptions

steps.b: The Fridays of the season run across the top. A ✓ means you already submitted that week. It opens on the current one.
HR is Home Run — grades and homework. BC is Bulls Commitment — behavior.
Everyone starts green. You only change the ones who had a problem.
The panel at the top shows who is currently on probation or suspended, so you can see it without hunting.

slides.title: Flag the issue and write the reason

steps.h: Tap HR or BC to flip it red
steps.b: A box opens asking what happened.
“Missing three homework assignments” or “was disrespectful to a substitute”. Short is fine.

steps.h: Parents read this word for word
steps.b: Your note is copied into the email that goes home. Write it the way you would say it to the parent.
The reason shows under the athlete’s name so you can see it at a glance.

steps.h: The button tells you the count
steps.b: It reads something like Submit week of Oct 9 · 2 flagged, so you can sanity-check before sending.
You can tap around all week. No email goes out and no standing changes until you submit.
A submitted week can be re-submitted, or reset if you need to start it over.

steps.h: A clean week still gets submitted
steps.b: If everyone was good, submit it anyway — that is what clears athletes off probation.

slides.title: The Home Run goal

steps.h: The bull shows where we are
steps.b: He rides the front of the bar and moves toward the finish line as the total climbs. When the goal is hit, the bar turns green.

steps.h: It is the whole school, not just your class
steps.b: Every athlete counts once per week. Your marks are part of one shared total, so it is a team effort across every homeroom.
The big number is home runs earned so far. The one after the slash is the goal. The small line tells you how many are still needed.

slides.note: Green HR = a home run for the school. Red HR = a missed one. That is the only thing that moves the bar — and the teacher food reward.

cards.b: Keep up with your work for the week. That is it. Do that and you scored one for the school.
There is no star player here. One athlete having a good week counts exactly as much as any other.

cards.h: Missing one is not the end
cards.b: A red week costs one home run and the bar keeps moving. Next week is a fresh chance.
Point at the school-wide total and tell them how close we are. Every green week they earn moves the school forward.

slides.title: The status ladder
slides.lede: A red on either button counts the same. It does not matter whether it was HR or BC, or whether both went red.

steps.b: Nothing happens, and any earlier trouble is wiped out.
The athlete still plays. The family and the coach get an email so everyone knows.

steps.h: Two bad weeks in a row → Suspended
steps.b: They sit out the next game. The family and coach get a different, clearer email.
They start over. A later bad week puts them back on probation — it does not stack into a longer ban.

slides.note: The two bad weeks must be back to back. A good week in between resets everything.

cards.b: Good standing the whole way. Nothing sent, nothing to do.
Probation after the bad week, then straight back to good standing. One email went home.
Probation, then suspended — they miss the next game.
Probation, cleared, probation again. Never suspended, because the bad weeks were not consecutive.

steps.h: HR and BC weigh the same
steps.b: One red is one bad week. Two reds in the same week is still just one bad week.

steps.h: Skipped weeks do not count against anyone
steps.b: Only weeks you actually submit are on the ladder.
It is recalculated from your submitted weeks, so fixing a mistake fixes the standing.

steps.h: You do not decide the punishment
steps.b: You report what happened in class. The ladder handles the rest.

stages.b: Flip HR or BC red and save the note.
That is the only moment mail goes out.

hub.b: Your note is the body. Clean athletes stay silent.

recipients.b: Primary. Both parent emails if the school has two.
A record of exactly what went out and when.
The team staff and athletic director see the same message.

branch.b: The athlete still shows on your screen with that tag — tell the office so they can add an address.

slides.title: What the family receives
slides.lede: The family sees your note exactly as you wrote it.

mail.subject: Jordan Smith — Probation Notice (Flag Football)
mail.headline: Jordan Smith
body: For the week of Sep 18, Jordan Smith was marked down and has been placed on probation.
mail.note: Missing three homework assignments this week.

slides.note: Suspension emails use the same layout — subject and status say Suspension, and the next game is named.

items: athleticsos.io/teacher — email, then your grade PIN.
Pick the week at the top.
Everyone starts green — only change the exceptions.
Submit, even if the whole week was clean.
Red on either one = one bad week.
Always write a clear, factual reason.
One bad week → probation, they still play.
Two in a row → suspended for the next game.
Email goes to parents, copied to you, the coaches and Kenny.
Every green HR is one home run for the school.
Only submitted weeks count — submit on time.
Hit it by season's end and Athletics provides food for the teachers (not students).
